hi.name: अध्याय 1: राष्ट्र निर्माण के चुनौतियाँ।
hi.summary: इस अध्याय में आजाद भारत द्वारा सामना की गई चुनौतियों के बारे में चर्चा की गई है, जैसे कि विभाजन, रियासती राज्यों के एकीकरण और राज्यों के पुनर्गठन।

mr.name: अध्याय 1: राष्ट्र निर्माणाच्या आव्हानांचा अभ्यास.

questions.stem: What was the main reason given for the Indian government's approach towards the princely states?
choices: To make the states rich
To ensure the unity of the country
To make the states independent
To allow the states to choose their own government
questions.solution: The main reason for the Indian government's approach was to ensure the unity of the country, as this was essential for maintaining a cohesive nation after independence. The other options do not align with the historical context of integrating princely states into a unified political structure. Making the states rich, allowing independence, or letting them choose their own government would have undermined national cohesion.

hi.stem: भारत सरकार के रियासतों के प्रति अपनी दृष्टि का मुख्य कारण क्या था?

देश के एकीकरण की गारंटी देना
राज्यों को स्वतंत्र बनाना
राज्यों को अपनी सरकार चुनने की अनुमति देना
hi.solution: भारत सरकार की दृष्टि का मुख्य कारण देश के एकीकरण की गारंटी देना था, क्योंकि स्वतंत्रता के बाद एक एकीकृत राष्ट्र बनाए रखना आवश्यक था। अन्य विकल्प रियासतों के एकीकरण के ऐतिहासिक संदर्भ के साथ मेल नहीं खाते। राज्यों को समृद्ध बनाना, उन्हें स्वतंत्र बनाना या उन्हें अपनी सरकार चुनने की अनुमति देना राष्ट्रीय एकता को कमजोर कर देता।
hi.critique: The Hindi translation accurately reflects the English original in meaning, structure, and terminology. All options are correctly translated, and the correct answer remains in the same position. The distractors remain incorrect, and the technical terms used are appropriate for a Hindi-medium curriculum.

questions.stem: What was the main concern of the Indian government regarding the Princely States after Independence?
choices: The rulers of the Princely States wanted to join Pakistan
The Princely States were not interested in democracy
There was a possibility of India being divided into small countries
The Princely States wanted to remain independent
questions.solution: The main concern was that the Princely States could lead to India being divided into smaller countries, which would weaken the nation's unity. The other options are incorrect because there is no evidence that the rulers specifically wanted to join Pakistan, or that the states were uninterested in democracy. The idea that they wanted independence was a potential result, not the primary worry.

hi.solution: मुख्य चिंता यह थी कि राज्य संभवतः भारत के छोटे देशों में विभाजित हो सकते थे, जो राष्ट्र की एकता को कमजोर कर सकता था। अन्य विकल्प गलत हैं क्योंकि कोई साक्ष्य नहीं है कि शासक विशेष रूप से पाकिस्तान में शामिल होना चाहते थे, या राज्य लोकतंत्र में रुचि नहीं रखते थे। यह विचार कि वे स्वतंत्र रहना चाहते थे, एक संभावित परिणाम था, न कि मुख्य चिंता।
hi.critique: The translation is accurate, maintains the original meaning, and uses appropriate Hindi terminology. The correct answer remains option 2, and the distractors are still incorrect.

questions.stem: What does the story of Salim Mirza suggest about the emotional impact of the Partition on individuals?
choices: It shows the economic benefits of migration
It highlights the loss of property and family
It emphasizes the political gains of the Muslim League
It illustrates the success of the Indian government's policies
questions.solution: The story of Salim Mirza highlights the emotional impact of the Partition by showing the loss of property and family, as his business declined and his home was taken by others. This reflects the deep personal suffering caused by the division. The other options focus on economic benefits, political gains, or government success, which are not supported by the emotional narrative of the story.

questions.stem: Why did the Indian government decide to negotiate with the rulers of the Princely States?
choices: To allow the rulers to choose their own alliances
To ensure the states joined India
To give the rulers more power over their own affairs
To avoid any form of conflict
questions.solution: The correct option is to ensure the states joined India, as the Indian government aimed to integrate the Princely States into the newly independent nation. The other options are incorrect because they suggest the government allowed rulers to maintain independence or avoid conflict, which were not the primary goals of the negotiations.

questions.stem: What was the main reason for Gandhi's fast in January 1948?
choices: To protest against the British government
To demand better treatment for Hindus
To bring peace between Hindus and Muslims
To celebrate the independence of India
questions.solution: Gandhi's fast in January 1948 was primarily aimed at promoting peace between Hindus and Muslims, as tensions and violence were rising during that time. This action was intended to encourage unity and reduce conflict between the two communities. The other options do not align with the historical context of his actions during that period.

questions.stem: What was the significance of the Standstill Agreement between the Nizam of Hyderabad and the Indian government?
choices: It allowed the Nizam to remain in power indefinitely
It allowed the Nizam to maintain a separate army
It delayed the integration of Hyderabad with India
It allowed Hyderabad to join Pakistan instead of India
questions.solution: The Standstill Agreement between the Nizam of Hyderabad and the Indian government in 1947 temporarily maintained the status quo, which delayed the formal integration of Hyderabad into India. This option is correct because the agreement was a temporary measure to allow time for negotiations. The other options are incorrect because the agreement did not grant the Nizam indefinite power, a separate army, or the right to join Pakistan.

They were indifferent to the political situation
